raw_text:
Here’s a concise, cohesive 12-week prenatal strength program summary tailored to your client: 30-year-old advanced lifter, 20 weeks pregnant at start, OB cleared for moderate strength, with constraints: no supine after week 16, no max attempts, no contact sports. Full gym access assumed. The plan emphasizes safe progression, a training feel (including bench-friendly pressing), core/pelvic floor integrity, cardio, and nutrition to maintain lean mass.

Overall structure
- Weekly frequency: 4 structured training days (A1, A2, B1, B2) with optional mobility/recovery day (E). Optional cardio days integrated around strength days (3–4 cardio sessions/week).
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–3: Foundation and technique
  - Weeks 4–6: Phase 2 – increased intensity while preserving safety (bench-friendly pressing emphasis)
  - Weeks 7–9: Phase 3 – maintenance with continued strength and safe progression
  - Weeks 10–12: Phase 4 – consolidation with peak-week considerations; Week 12 focuses on submaximal testing options instead of 1RM

Weekly session format (per training day)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes light cardio + mobility for the target region
- Main lifts: 3–4 sets of 6–10 reps (lower/upper emphasis) with RPE targets
- Accessory work: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps
- Core/pelvic floor: integrated per session (Pal lof/anti-rotation and bracing throughout)
- Cardio: 20–40 minutes moderate, 3–4 days/week; paired with strength sessions or on separate days
- Recovery: mobility, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor activation; hydration and nutrition aligned with training

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and technique
- Emphasis: technique, consistent breathing, pelvic-floor engagement, light-to-moderate loads
- Lower Day A1
  - Goblet Squat: 3x8–10
  - Romanian Deadlift (DB or Barbell): 3x8–10
  - Split Squat (DB or barbell front rack): 3x8–10 per leg
  - Hip Thrust/Glute Bridge: 3x10–12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x8–10 per side; dead bug or side plank 3x20–30s
  - Optional hamstring curl: 2x12
- Upper Day A2 (Push emphasis with bench-friendly options)
  - Incline Dumbbell Press 30–45° or Chest-Supported Press: 3x8–10
  - Lat Pulldown/Assisted Pull-Up: 3x8–10
  - Seated Row: 3x8–10
  - Chest Press (incline or machine): 3x8–10
  - Push-ups (incline/elevated) if tolerated: 3x6–10
  - Triceps Pushdown: 2–3x10–12
  - Biceps Curl: 2x10–12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x12 per side
- Lower Day B1 (tempo/technique)
  - Front Squat or Squat: 3x6–8; tempo 3–0–1
  - Deadlift variation (trap bar or light conventional): 3x6–8
  - Step-Ups/Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8–10 per leg
  - Hip Abductor/Adductor: 2x12–15
  - Glute Bridge: 3x12–15
  - Core: Dead Bug 3x12
- Upper Day B2 (Accessory/volume)
  - Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press or Arnold Press: 3x8–10
  - Cable Row: 3x8–10
  - Chest Fly (low load): 3x10–12
  - Face Pulls: 3x12–15
  - Lateral Raises: 2x12–15
  - Core: Pallof press 3x12 per side
- Cardio: 20–30 minutes, moderate intensity; option for longer easy day if energy allows
- Nutrition: maintain protein 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; ensure 250–350 kcal/day surplus if OB guidance allows; hydration 2.5–3.5 L/day

Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Phase 2 – push intensity, maintain form, bench emphasis
- Core principle: maintain core engagement, no supine loading after week 16; tempo variations and slightly higher RPE on main lifts
- Lower Day A1
  - Goblet Squat: 4x8–10; +2–5% load if technique solid; tempo 2–0–2
  - Romanian Deadlift: 4x8–10; tempo 2–1–2
  - Split Squat: 3–4x8–10 per leg; add light DB/KB
  - Hip Thrust/Glute Bridge: 3x10–12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x12 per side with slow peak hold
  - Optional hamstring curl: 2x12
- Lower Day B1 (Tempo emphasis)
  - Front Squat or Squat: 4x6–8; tempo 3–0–1
  - Deadlift variation: 3–4x6–8
  - Step-Ups/Bulgarian Split Squat: 3–4x8–10
  - Hip Abductor/Adductor: 2x12–15
  - Glute Bridge: 3x12–15
  - Core: Dead Bug 3x12
- Upper Day A2 (Push emphasis with bench options)
  - Incline Dumbbell Press (30–45°) or Chest-Supported Press: 4x8–10
  - Lat Pulldown/Assisted Pull-Up: 4x8–10
  - Seated Row: 3–4x8–10
  - Chest Press (machine or incline): 3x8–10
  - Push-Ups (incline/elevated) 3x6–10
  - Triceps Pushdown: 3x10–12
  - Biceps Curl: 2x10–12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x12 per side
- Upper Day B2 (Bench emphasis continuation)
  - DB Floor Press or Seated Dumbbell Press: 3–4x8–10
  - Cable Row/Barbell Row: 3–4x8–10
  - Shoulder Press (seated/incline): 3x8–10
  - Chest Fly (low load): 3x10–12
  - Lateral Raises: 2–3x12–15
  - Core: Pallof press variations 3x12 per side
- Cardio: 3–4 sessions; one longer steady-state day (40–45 min) if energy allows; optional light intervals 1 day/week
- Nutrition: maintain protein 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; 250–350 kcal surplus if appropriate; post-workout nutrition within 60–90 min
- Recovery: prioritize sleep (7–9 hours), diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor activation

Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength maintenance with safety and form
- Core focus: anti-rotation/anti-extension and bracing emphasis; avoid high intra-abdominal pressure tasks
- Lower Day A1: 4x6–8 goblet/front squats; RPE 7–8 on main sets
- Lower Day B1: 4x6–8 front squat/squat; tempo 3–0–1
- Upper Day A2: 4x6–8 incline press/bench-friendly variations; RPE 7–8; seated rows
- Upper Day B2: 3–4x8–10 incline/dumbbell presses; 3x8–10 rows
- Core: maintain 2–3 core sessions/week with Pallof press, side planks, dead bug progressions
- Cardio: 3–4 sessions; maintain 20–35 minutes; include one longer day if energy allows
- Nutrition: protein 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; caloric intake aligned with OB guidance; emphasize post-workout protein

Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Consolidation and peak-week planning; Week 12 peak-testing considerations (no true 1RM)
- Peak-week concept: no true 1RM; use submaximal testing or RPE-based assessments to gauge readiness
- Lower Day A1: 3–4x6–8 goblet squats; maintain form
- Lower Day B1: 3–4x6–8 leg press/front squat variation
- Upper Day A2: 3–4x8–10 incline presses; seated rows
- Upper Day B2: 3–4x8–10 bench-friendly pressing variations; rows
- Core: consistent anti-rotation and bracing work; maintain 2–3 core sessions
- Cardio: 3–4 sessions; one lighter week might be included for recovery
- Peak-week testing options (no max attempts):
  - Option A (tech + RP): 2–3 lifts at one hard but controlled set (RPE 8–8.5) with 3–5 reps; track load and reps
  - Option B (RIR): 2 lifts with 3 sets of 4–6 reps at loads leaving 1–2 RIR; no effort to failure
  - Option C (movement quality): 4–6 exercises in a controlled circuit, 45 seconds per station, moderate effort
- Post-testing: back off to conservative maintenance loads for Weeks 12–13; emphasize technique and recovery

Key safety notes present throughout
- Supine risk: avoid supine loading after week 16; if needed earlier, use incline 30–45°, seated presses, or chest-supported variations
- No max attempts: avoid true 1RMs; use submax tests or RPE-based approaches
- Pelvic floor and diastasis: maintain diaphragmatic breathing, avoid straining; monitor for doming or pelvic discomfort
- Symptoms: stop and reassess with OB if dizziness, chest pain, excessive fatigue, vaginal bleeding, or reduced fetal movement occurs
- Hydration and heat: stay hydrated; avoid overheating; adjust workouts in hot conditions
- Nausea/heartburn: adjust meals timing and meal size around workouts

Nutrition and cardio integration recap
- Protein target: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; evenly distributed
- Carbohydrates: around training for energy; prioritize complex carbs; fiber-rich foods
- Fats: include omega-3 sources
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day or more with activity
- Supplements: prenatal vitamin; DHA as advised; iron if indicated; consult OB
- Cardio: 3–4 days/week of low-to-moderate intensity; variety (walking, cycling, elliptical, swimming); avoid high-impact or contact activities

Progress tracking and adjustments
- Keep a simple log: lift weights, sets, reps, RPE, symptoms
- Weekly check-ins: track energy, nausea, sleep, mood; adjust caloric/protein targets accordingly
- Reassess every 4 weeks: technique, load progression, and comfort
- Client feedback: adjust exercise selection if due to diastasis, pelvic pain, or shoulder issues

I can tailor it further to her lift preferences and equipment (dumbbells, machines, incline bench) and to any obstetric notes you have.
